title: Which data movement tool fits you?

questions.hint: This one choice cuts the list down fast.

options.label: Files and folders
options.why: you are copying files, not rows

options.label: A whole database, once or kept in sync
App and database data for reports
options.why: you load rows into a warehouse or lake

options.label: Database changes as a stream of events
options.why: you want each change as an event

questions.q: Where does the data need to land?

options.label: AWS storage or an AWS database
Google Cloud Storage
options.why: DataSync writes to S3, EFS and FSx, and Storage Mover targets Azure only

options.label: Azure
options.why: DataSync writes to AWS storage and Storage Transfer Service moves into Cloud Storage

options.label: Another cloud, a warehouse or my own place
options.why: Google Storage Transfer Service and Azure Storage Mover only write to their own cloud

questions.hint: Free software still costs servers and people.

options.label: A vendor runs it for me
options.why: rclone and Debezium have no hosted service

options.label: My team runs it
options.why: you are happy to run it yourself

questions.q: How fresh must the data be?

options.label: Every few minutes
options.why: Fivetran documents 15-minute syncs on Standard and 1 minute on Enterprise

options.label: Within seconds
options.why: Debezium documents millisecond delays for MySQL or PostgreSQL, while Airbyte CDC syncs are scheduled and AWS DMS gives no CDC latency promise

questions.q: What kind of bill suits you?

options.label: Free software, I pay with my time
options.why: no licence fee, you pay for servers and staff time

options.label: A flat rate per GB or per hour
options.why: the meter is volume or hours, not rows

options.label: A usage meter that grows with changes
options.why: you can budget for a per-row or per-credit meter

datasync.name: AWS DataSync
datasync.summary: A file transfer service for moving file or object data into AWS storage.
datasync.bestWhen: your files are headed into S3, EFS or FSx and you want one flat per-GB rate.
datasync.watchOut: it moves files, not databases, and S3 request and storage fees come on top.

gts.name: Google Storage Transfer Service
gts.summary: Moves data from S3, Azure Blob Storage, on-premises systems, HDFS and public URLs into Cloud Storage.
gts.bestWhen: you have large one-off or recurring copies into Cloud Storage.
gts.watchOut: no SLA for transfer performance, it is tuned for transfers above 1 TiB, and network and storage fees apply on top.

azmover.name: Azure Storage Mover
azmover.summary: A fully managed service for moving file shares and S3 buckets into Azure Storage.
azmover.bestWhen: you are moving file shares into Azure and want a service with no fee of its own.
azmover.watchOut: Azure targets only, and storage, transactions and network are still billed.

rclone.name: rclone
rclone.summary: A free command-line file copier that works across more than 70 cloud storage products.
rclone.bestWhen: a command line does not scare you and you want one tool across many storage providers.
rclone.watchOut: no hosted service, no SLA stated, and you add cron or similar for scheduling. Files only.

dms.name: AWS Database Migration Service
dms.summary: Moves databases into AWS, as a one-time move or ongoing replication, with wide source support.
dms.bestWhen: you are moving or replicating a database into AWS.
dms.watchOut: no CDC latency SLA, not real-time, no Iceberg target, and you size and watch the replication server.

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A vendor-run pipeline service with 700+ connectors and a free plan up to 500,000 monthly active rows.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want someone else to run the pipeline and can budget for a per-row meter.
fivetran.watchOut: paid per-row rates are in a separate table, usage includes deletes, and self-hosting is only an Enterprise Hybrid option.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: Over 600 connectors, a free self-hosted Core and a credit-based Cloud.
airbyte.bestWhen: you want lots of connectors and scheduled syncs are fine.
airbyte.watchOut: CDC syncs run on a schedule, not as a continuous stream, and Core uses the source-available Elastic License 2.0.

debezium.name: Debezium
debezium.summary: A free engine that reads database change logs and turns each change into an event.
debezium.bestWhen: you want log-based CDC and have people to operate it.
debezium.watchOut: it is an engine, not a finished pipeline, so you build the path to your warehouse or lake. The Iceberg sink is community-maintained.
